scenario.figure_or_table: Table IV, row 'Ours' (thermal map in Fig. 10(b), PDF page 12)
scenario.description: ThermoDSE-optimized 2.5D chiplet DNN accelerator: 5x4 NPU cores split into 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm inter-chiplet spacing, 240 GB/s NoC/NoP bandwidth, 1024 KB uniform buffer and 208x112 systolic array per core. Reported results: peak temperature 74.8 C, energy 59.8 mJ, delay 2.01 ms, yield 0.911, EDYP 132.2. Thermal evaluation used HotSpot 6.0 steady-state with a 300 mm2 interposer area limit and a 75 C peak-temperature limit. The packet contains no per-block coordinates, dimensions, or power values.
scenario.architecture: Chiplet-based DNN accelerator (Arch-S, fine-grained task orchestration across chiplets): 5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 1024 KB uniform buffer, 208x112 systolic array, 240 GB/s NoC bandwidth; 14 nm scaled, 1.8 GHz
scenario.workload: AR/VR multi-DNN mix: ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, MobileNetv2, Yolov2, U-Net, BERT-Small (batch sizes per Table III)
scenario.operating_point: 1.8 GHz, 14 nm, HotSpot 6.0 steady-state, ambient 45 C, convection resistance 0.4 K/W, 300 mm2 interposer limit, 75 C peak limit; reported peak temperature 74.8 C

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 6.0 steady-state thermal simulation (PDF p.4, p.7) using component-wise average power, floorplan and material properties. Performance, energy and yield come from a custom simulator with fine-grained µtask orchestration. Ambient 45 C, convection resistance 0.4 K/W, TIM, heat spreader and heat sink properties adopted from TESA (PDF p.7, p.9).
original_setup.optimizer: TED (transductive experimental design) initialization plus SCBO (scalable constrained Bayesian optimization, BoTorch) minimizing EDYP = E x D / Y under a 75 C peak-temperature limit and a 300 mm2 interposer-area limit (PDF p.7-9). Compared with SA (TESA) and PPO-based RL (Chiplet-Gym) (PDF p.12, Table V).
original_setup.controller: No runtime thermal controller. DVFS is discussed as unsuitable (PDF p.3). Thermal management is design-time only: greedy thermal-aware task mapping puts high-power µtasks on corner cores and low-power ones on center cores (PDF p.5), plus inter-chiplet spacing as a cooling knob.
original_setup.benchmark: AR/VR multi-DNN mix of ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, MobileNetv2, Yolov2, U-Net and BERT-Small (Table III, PDF p.9), run sequentially at 1.8 GHz in 14 nm. Selected scenario: the 'Ours' row of Table IV (PDF p.10): 5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 1024 KB uniform buffer, 208x112 systolic array, 240 GB/s NoC. Reported energy 59.8 mJ, delay 2.01 ms, yield 0.911, EDYP 132.2. Thermal map in Fig. 10(b) (PDF p.12).

thermal_observable.location: Peak temperature of the chiplet-based accelerator, from HotSpot 6.0 on the interposer-level floorplan of the ThermoDSE-optimized design
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum (peak) steady-state temperature over the floorplan, using component-wise average power over the AR/VR workload mix

physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a 2.5D multi-chiplet system on an interposer with NoP/D2D links, die-to-die spacing (ICS 2.3 mm) and a TIM/heat spreader/heat sink stack. A simple 2D single-die runner cannot reproduce the inter-chiplet lateral coupling, interposer heat spreading or NoP power distribution.

The power input is an average derived from analytical energy/latency models over a sequential multi-DNN workload. It is not a transient power trace, and the paper models no transient thermal behavior, only steady state.

The paper does not publish per-block floorplan coordinates, block dimensions or per-block power for the selected design. Only aggregate parameters are given: core/chiplet counts, ICS, buffer size, systolic array size, and total energy and delay. A block-level replication is therefore impossible.

The optimizer is TED+SCBO Bayesian optimization co-optimizing architecture and task mapping, with no runtime controller. A Studio runner has no equivalent optimizer, so only the thermal solve could be exercised.
The cooling model (convection resistance 0.4 K/W, 45 C ambient, TESA material properties) and the HotSpot 6.0 package stack may differ from the Studio's bundled material and package assumptions.
Reliability is not modeled beyond the 75 C peak limit. Yield is modeled analytically from die area and is unrelated to thermal reliability.

studio_assumptions: No paper-derived floorplan exists, so any runner placement would be a separately generated illustrative 2D layout with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper facts.
Studio uses its own bundled package and material stack, which is not guaranteed to match the paper's HotSpot 6.0 interposer/TIM/spreader/heat-sink configuration (TESA properties).
Studio runs a 2D thermal solve, not the paper's 2.5D interposer model.
Any one-row power trace would be illustrative only, and Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 74.8 C.

methods.note: The method claims are supported by the text. HotSpot 6.0 steady state (p.4, p.7), TED+SCBO under 75 C and 300 mm2 (p.7-9), fine-grained uTask orchestration with corner-first thermal mapping (p.5), and average power as energy/(delay x period) (Eq. 19, p.7) all match the PDF. However, the paper's thermal model is a 2.5D interposer stack with NoP, TIM, spreader and heat sink (Fig. 6, p.7). The extraction itself lists this as an essential mismatch, yet it still sets steady_2d_relevant=true and experiment.kind=custom_2d_steady. Those two choices contradict the extraction's own essential mismatches.

code.note: No code, repository, supplementary data or availability statement appears in the supplied pages (pp.1-14). The only URLs are refs [1] and [36] and the arXiv source. The asset list is empty, so there is no pinned evidence for the simulator, the TED+SCBO implementation or the HotSpot configs.

parameters.note: Table IV 'Ours' (p.10) matches the extraction: 74.8 C, 59.8 mJ, 2.01 ms, 0.911 yield, EDYP 132.2, 5x4 cores, 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 240 GB/s, 1024 KB, 208x112. Conditions on p.9 also match: 14 nm, 1.8 GHz, 45 C ambient, 0.4 K/W, 300 mm2, 75 C. The Fig. 11 vector ordering on p.12 is consistent with the XX,YY,Xcut,Ycut reading. These are aggregate parameters only. The 1 KB = 1024 B convention and the EDYP units (mJ*ms) are the extraction's inference, not stated in the paper. Only the Table IV numbers were checked against the extracted text, because no figure images were supplied.

config.note: There is no paper-derived floorplan, block coordinates, block dimensions or per-block power for the selected design. TIM, spreader and heat-sink properties are only cited to TESA [12] (p.7) with no values. Compute-die, I/O-die and interposer areas for the 2-chiplet design are not given. data.note: Only totals are tabulated: energy, delay, yield and peak temperature. No per-block power exists for any floorplan block in the same scenario, no transient trace and no hotspot location. Fig. 10(a) and Fig. 10(b) (p.12) are available only as extracted text captions, with no rendered images. They were not visually verified and no digitization was done. The area fractions (49%, 17.6%, 14.2% less buffer area) come from p.12 text only.

findings.reason: The locator cites the Fig. 11 caption (p.12) as support for the 2.3 mm ICS of the Table IV 'Ours' scenario. That caption describes a different scenario: a 200 mm2 area limit and design [4,4,1,2,2.3,144,112,1024KB,240] with 4x4 cores, 2.27 ms, 60 mJ and yield 0.943. The ICS match is coincidental, so this is a scenario mismatch and the citation is invalid.

assessment.summary: Scenario: ThermoDSE (W7167828524), Table IV 'Ours' row, a 2.5D chiplet DNN accelerator (5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 240 GB/s, 1024 KB buffer, 208x112 array). The paper reports a 74.8 C peak temperature from HotSpot 6.0 steady state against a 75 C limit. The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, and the experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace. Studio did NOT run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass are both false. The stated reason is that a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, while the extraction left floorplan and power_w empty because the paper publishes no per-block coordinates, dimensions or powers. No pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes were used, so there is no generated placement, no input.flp and no input.ptrace, and no source commit applies. No linked assets, code or repositories were found. The gate sets the final verdict and comparison_valid=false, so there is no Studio temperature to compare with the paper's 74.8 C and no replication is claimed. Only qualitative reading is supported: the design is reported as just under its thermal limit, with greedy corner-core mapping and inter-chiplet spacing as design-time cooling knobs. The conclusion is unverified, since the adversarial checks and independent review are unresolved.
limitations: Studio was not run, so there is no simulated result and no numerical comparison to 74.8 C.
Inputs are missing: no floorplan blocks, no per-block power (only total energy 59.8 mJ and delay 2.01 ms), and no package or material parameters (TIM, spreader, sink cited to TESA but not given).

Physical mismatch (essential): the paper uses a 2.5D interposer with two chiplets, a 2.3 mm gap and NoP links, while a 2D single-die runner cannot capture lateral inter-chiplet coupling or interposer spreading.
Regime mismatch: the paper's power is a workload-averaged steady-state value from analytical energy/latency models, and there is no transient trace or transient result.
Boundary mismatch: the paper uses HotSpot 6.0 with 45 C ambient, 0.4 K/W convection and TESA materials, which may differ from Studio's bundled stack.

Location and aggregation: the 74.8 C is a floorplan-wide peak with no stated hotspot location, so it could only match a Studio value with the same location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions.
No pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace data or source commit was used, and no generated placement exists; any future placement would be illustrative and not paper-derived.
Optimizer (TED+SCBO) and task mapping were not reproduced.
The gate did not pass (artifact search found no links, and adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved), so the claim is not independently verified and no exact replication is claimed.
